_comment_family: Great Vibes is a copperplate script and it ships as one style - there
is no Bold and no italic of it anywhere, so unlike the Cormorant pack
beside it there is no sibling for a bare family name to be confused
with. Name ID 1 is 'Great Vibes' and that is what gets declared, the
same position brittany-signature and special-elite are in.
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass. A script hand has
no weight axis to ask along: there is one hand, and asking a browser
for a bold of it would only invite it to smear the one there is.
_comment_metrics: Two numbers about this face reach the channel that uses it, and both
are about how much room it takes rather than how it looks.
It is drawn far taller and deeper than its em. Across the lower case
the ink runs from 629 units above the baseline to -351 below, on a
1000-unit em: at the Snapchat preset's 40px that is 25.2px up and
14.0px down, where Cormorant Garamond's own lower case gives 29.0 and
-11.3. Set together the two faces therefore ask for a band about 43px
tall, against the 27px a row of Telegraf capitals asks for on Hall of
Femme - which is what the card behind a caption on this channel is
sized to (see the shared band in js/text.js, and the block height note
The capitals are the extreme case and are why that channel does not
use them. They reach 861 up and -400 down - 34.4px and -16.0px at 40 -
and they are enormously wide with it: nineteen capitals measure 44%
wider here than the same capitals in Cormorant. A swash capital is
drawn to open a word, not to fill one.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is

describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.

_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before anything is
drawn. They are still chosen, and here the choice is as consequential
as brittany-signature's: this is a joined script, and every heavy
display cut the rest of this folder falls through is the furthest
possible thing from it. Impact behind this face would not be a
degraded highlight, it would be a different channel.
So the stack stays a script all the way down, and it starts one step
nearer than brittany-signature's does. Edwardian Script ITC arrives
with Microsoft Office and is a copperplate hand like this one - a
formal, steeply sloped, high-contrast script rather than a casual
handwriting - so on a machine that has ever had Office the stand-in is
the same KIND of writing. Segoe Script is behind it as the one hand
every Windows 10 and 11 can be relied on to have, even though it is a
casual hand and not a copperplate, and the generic `cursive` is the
last thing that is still a script rather than a grotesque.
